channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Hao Zhang, Matthew Otten

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Computational method for electronic structure calculations, relevant for strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #computationalmethod #electronicstructure #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: Electronic structure calculations usually need a good starting guess, often unavailable for strongly correlated systems. The authors develop an auto-initializing algorithm that efficiently finds accurate ground states from random Slater determinants.

item.title: [9] Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Gil Young Cho, Yeongkwan Kim

Authors: Kimoon Higashihira Han, Dongju Hwang, Dongsin Kim, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Chris Jozwiak

Tags: #chargedensitywave

Abstract: The authors show that the subcomponents of the charge density wave in 1T-TiSe₂ are unequal and set in one by one, beginning with an unexpected unidirectional state.
